# `typing.json`

**Generated by:** hand-classification (no dedicated script) — read `silence-frames/*.png` and write this file directly. See the **summera-youtube-shorts** skill, step 3.
**Consumed by:** `src/Root.tsx` (`calculateMetadata`, fallback path) via `buildTimeline()`; `scripts/build-timeline.ts`

Which of the silent stretches from `silence.json` are actually on-screen
activity (typing, loading, scrolling) worth keeping at a sped-up rate, vs.
pure dead air worth cutting entirely. There's no ML/heuristic for this —
`export-silence-frames.ts` samples one thumbnail per second across every
silence segment, and a human (or Claude, reading the frames) classifies each
timestamp by eye.

```json
{
  "typingSegments": [
    {"start": 27.061688, "end": 28.079062},
    {"start": 30.336, "end": 30.893062}
  ],
  "source": "public/assets/20260724_youtube_posts.mp4",
  "labeledBy": "claude-vision",
  "notes": "Keyboard visible in silence-frames at t=28,32,34 ..."
}
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `typingSegments` | `{start, end}[]` | seconds; ranges to keep at `typingSpeed`x instead of cutting |
| `source` | `string` | path to the video that was classified, for provenance |
| `labeledBy` | `string` | who/what classified it (e.g. `"claude-vision"`) |
| `notes` | `string` | free-text reasoning — which frames showed what, and why gaps between sampled frames were bridged or not |

Where a `typingSegment` overlaps a `speechSegment`, `buildTimeline()` gives
speech priority (trims the typing span down or drops it). Anything not
covered by `speechSegments` or `typingSegments` is pure silence and gets cut.

**Excising unwanted content from inside a stretch:** since anything
uncovered is cut, splitting one `typingSegments` range into two adjacent
ones with a gap removes whatever's in that gap from the final video
entirely — not just skipped-past, gone. Useful for a transient in-app error
message, a UI glitch, or any other flash of on-screen content that shouldn't
ship, sitting inside an otherwise-worth-keeping loading/typing stretch:

```json
{
  "typingSegments": [
    {"start": 18.12325, "end": 25.1},
    {"start": 28.9, "end": 37.051313}
  ]
}
```

Here the original single 18.12–37.05s loading stretch had a 25.1–28.9s
window (an "AI service temporarily unavailable" error blip, pinpointed by
sampling extra frames at 0.5s intervals around it) sliced out — that window
is simply cut, not sped up. Always rerun `scripts/build-timeline.ts` after
an edit like this (see `timeline.md`) — it isn't optional.
